question: Now step back to where the game puts you when you are pointing a robot at squares. From up here, which one still tells you what is ready?
note: The same plot at the same moment, seen from the height the camera rises to when it hands you a machine to direct — about half the size the game is normally drawn at. The teaching mode's own dimming is deliberately not in the shot: what is being asked is whether the cue survives the distance, not how it competes with the grey.

drafts.name: off · as today
drafts.blurb: the fourth picture and nothing else — the game as it is today

drafts.name: A · the ripe ones nod
drafts.blurb: a ready plant sways, and no two squares sway together

drafts.name: B · the ripe ones stand up
drafts.blurb: a ready plant is heavier, sits proud of the soil and throws a shadow

drafts.name: C · the ripe ones give off their own colour
drafts.blurb: a soft bloom in the crop's own ripe colour — gold wheat, red tomato

drafts.name: D · a gentler sway, and the glow
drafts.blurb: half A's sway, slower, over C's light — the two together, quieter
